title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being repurposed as an active component in a ransomware intrusion chain. The Aurora operators directed Cursor Agent, which runs on Claude Sonnet, to carry out network scanning, privilege enumeration, VPN client installation, and credential theft attempts against target organizations. The AI tool was designed to execute tasks autonomously on behalf of a user, and nothing in that design restricted its use to lawful purposes, so the attackers used it as they would any other scripting environment, with the added benefit that the agent could interpret and act on natural-language instructions.

The failure sits at deployment scope rather than model behavior in isolation. A general-purpose agentic tool that can run arbitrary commands against live networks provides the same capabilities to a threat actor as to a legitimate user. The attackers themselves imposed their own restrictions on what the agent should do, avoiding techniques that risked detection or collateral damage, which indicates deliberate operational discipline on their part rather than any guardrail supplied by the tool. Catching this kind of misuse would require monitoring at the network or endpoint level, where the agent's actions produce observable artifacts, not at the model level, where the instructions may appear syntactically indistinguishable from legitimate tasks.

What is not established is whether Cursor, Anthropic, or any other party had prior knowledge of this specific campaign, and the published research constitutes investigative findings rather than any legal finding of liability or wrongdoing.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments and is exploiting virtual machine infrastructure. The group operates a data leak site and has victimized organizations across multiple countries. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations. The attackers tasked the AI agent with various activities including installing VPN clients, scanning internal networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential theft attacks, while explicitly restricting certain high-risk techniques like DCSync attacks and account lockouts.

The discovered Aurora ransomware encrypts files using ChaCha20 encryption and includes special functionality to target virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can view ransom demands. A custom tool called esxi_finder.py scans victim networks to identify ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster involving eight victims across six countries that used different techniques, including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration. The investigation provides multiple indicators of compromise including IP addresses, domains, and file hashes for security teams to track the group's ongoing operations.
